purpose: Degarelix is used to treat advanced prostate cancer. It works by lowering the amount of testosterone in your body, which helps slow down or stop the growth of prostate cancer cells. It is given as an injection by your healthcare provider.
how_it_works: Prostate cancer cells often need testosterone to grow. Degarelix blocks signals in your brain that tell your body to make testosterone. By quickly lowering testosterone levels, it helps keep the cancer from spreading or getting worse.
common_side_effects: Hot flashes or sweating, injection site reactions like pain, redness, or swelling, tiredness, weight gain, decreased sex drive, and problems getting or keeping an erection are the most common side effects. Some men may also notice breast tenderness or swelling.
warnings: This medication can affect your heart rhythm, so tell your doctor if you have any heart problems. It may cause bone thinning over time, increasing your risk of fractures. It can also raise blood sugar or increase the risk of diabetes. Tell your doctor about all your medications and medical history before starting degarelix. Do not use this medication in women or children.
typical_dosing: You will receive two injections under the skin in your belly area on your first visit, giving a starting dose of 240 mg total. After that, you will get one injection of 80 mg every 28 days to keep your testosterone levels low. All injections are given by your doctor or nurse at a clinic.
